lines.trans: Did you see what just happened in the hall?
Our bartender boldly stepped up to the critic's table.
This critic was rudely insulting our Nastya again.

words.gloss: to hurt, to offend, to bully

lines.trans: Kostya did not start tolerating such insolent behavior.

words.gloss: to bear, to put up with; to hold on

lines.trans: What, did the guest order a drink from the bar now?
Exactly, he received an order to the fullest program!
Kostya poured a glass right onto his suit!
Our quiet bartender turned out to be a real brave hero.

words.gloss: to turn out to be, find oneself

lines.trans: Now this important critic sits completely wet.
But the chef will be terribly angry because of the scandal.
Victoria is already quickly running into the dining hall.
A very swift dismissal definitely threatens Kostya right now.
At least he courageously protected his beloved girl!

words.gloss: but on the other hand, to make up for it

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bar, pub' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Our bar is closing.

examples.text: Проверьте все бары и старых друзей.
examples.trans: Check all the bars and old friends.
It is already morning. Our bar is closing.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'bartender', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Бармен наливает холодную воду в стакан.
examples.trans: The bartender pours cold water into the glass.
The bartender poured the wine.

examples.text: Бармен, принесите нам бокал белого вина!
examples.trans: Bartender, bring us a glass of white wine!

meanings.en: to run (in one direction), to flee, to escape
meanings.note: irregular mixed conjugation: бегу, бежишь, ..., бегут

examples.trans: Run, Marina, before it's too late!
Where are you running so fast?

examples.text: Надо бежать! Беги в деревню к маме.
examples.trans: You need to run! Run to the village to your mum's.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.trans: He drives fast.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Давай работай быстрее, гости уже давно ждут заказ!
examples.trans: Come on, work faster, the guests have been waiting for their order for a long time!

meanings.note: moving or capable of moving at high speed

examples.trans: We need fast internet.

examples.text: Они сказали, что устанавливают быстрый интернет.
examples.trans: They said that they were installing fast internet.

examples.text: Большое спасибо за вашу быструю помощь!
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your quick help!

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.trans: It's an important question.
I have important business.

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to see', forming an aspectual pair with 'увидеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = see?') (drawing attention) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

examples.text: Ты видишь, сколько гостей сегодня вечером сидит в зале?
examples.trans: Do you see how many guests are sitting in the hall tonight?

meanings.en: to pour out, empty, dump (liquid) onto
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'лить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to pour out', forming an aspectual pair with 'выливать'.

examples.text: Он мне вылил кашу на голову!
examples.trans: He poured porridge on my head!
Pour the cold water out of the cup.

examples.text: Марина! Что вы сделали? Он мне вылил кашу на голову!
examples.trans: Marina! What have you done? He poured porridge on my head!

meanings.note: a brave person; also the main character of a story

examples.trans: Now you're a hero.
He's a real hero.

examples.text: Всё, теперь ты герой? И можно только пить?
examples.trans: So now you're a hero? And all you have to do is drink?

meanings.note: Abstract masculine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'guest'.

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.
You have visitors!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to threaten, face', paired with 'пригрозить'.

examples.trans: A prison sentence threatens for this.
He shook his fist at us.

examples.text: За порчу исторического наследия грозит реальная тюрьма.
examples.trans: For damaging historical heritage, real prison threatens.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Don't talk so rudely.
That's rude.

examples.text: А что вы так грубо разговариваете?
examples.trans: Why are you talking so rudely?

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'girl'.

examples.text: Девушки, как я, у тебя не будет!
examples.trans: You'll never have a girl like me!
This is my girlfriend Lyolya.
She's my girlfriend.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'order', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('booking') (commission or reservation) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я делаю всё точно по вашему заказу.
examples.trans: I do everything exactly according to your order.
In the kitchen they are preparing this order.
The waiter took the order.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to order', paired with 'заказывать'.

examples.trans: Maybe we should order?
We ordered tea and sandwiches.

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно. Может, закажем?
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free. Maybe we should order?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'hall', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('living room') (regional/colloquial) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Please enter the courtroom.
A big hall.
Understood. And who is managing the dining room?

зато.gloss: but on the other hand, to make up for it

meanings.en: but on the other hand, at least
meanings.note: introduces a compensating positive fact

examples.text: Четыре по алгебре, зато по физкультуре пятёрка.
examples.trans: A four in algebra, but a five in gym.
The flat is small, but at least it's in the centre.

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Сейчас зато аппетит нагуляем.
examples.trans: No big deal. At least we'll walk up an appetite now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'щитить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to protect, to defend', paired with 'защищать'.

examples.trans: He will be able to protect me.

examples.text: Я думаю, что у меня есть мужчина. Он сможет меня защитить.
examples.trans: I think that I have a man. He will be able to protect me.

examples.text: Мы должны защитить эту историческую стену.
examples.trans: We must protect this historical wall.

meanings.note: злая собака = vicious dog; а почему вы такая злая? = why are you so hostile?

examples.trans: Why are you so hostile?
Don't be so cross.
I am an evil enemy.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.trans: The town hall called me.
He's from Moscow.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'because of' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('from behind') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'to' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.
I'm going to Mum's.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'suit', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('costume, outfit') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: A very bad suit!
This is my wedding suit, actually!
In a waffle-cone costume.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'critic, reviewer' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The restaurant critic praised the bartender.

examples.text: К нам сегодня приедет ресторанный критик.
examples.trans: A restaurant critic will come to us today.
A restaurant critic is sitting in the hall.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').
Secondary conversational sense ('beloved, darling') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой!
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake!
This is my favourite book.

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой! До вечера, Марина.
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake! See you tonight, Marina.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'wet', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Теперь этот критик весь мокрый сидит в зале.
examples.trans: Now this critic sits completely wet in the dining room.

examples.text: Теперь этот важный критик весь мокрый сидит.
examples.trans: Now this important critic sits completely wet.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: showing a lack of respect in a rude or aggressive manner

examples.trans: That was a very insolent act.
What an insolent, vile thief!
Be quiet right now, insolent rump!

meanings.note: Derived masculine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'drink'.

examples.trans: The bartender made a delicious cold beverage.
A cold drink.

examples.text: Ты совсем не пьёшь крепкие напитки?
examples.trans: Do you not drink strong drinks at all?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').
Secondary conversational sense ('present, current') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: This is real success!
He is a true friend.

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.trans: I love our town.
This is our flat.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'dining' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: The dining hall of the restaurant.

examples.text: Она снова убежит в обеденный зал.
examples.trans: She will run off to the dining hall again.

examples.text: Виктория уже быстро бежит в обеденный зал.
examples.trans: Victoria is already quickly running into the dining hall.

обижать.gloss: to hurt, to offend, to bully

meanings.en: to hurt, to mistreat, to offend
meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ижать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hurt, to offend, to bully', paired with 'обидеть'.

examples.trans: But hurting children isn't right.
Never hurt little ones.

examples.text: Ребята, я понимаю, работа у вас такая. Но детей обижать нехорошо.
examples.trans: Guys, I understand, that's the job you have. But hurting children isn't right.

оказаться.gloss: to turn out to be, find oneself

meanings.en: to turn out to be, prove to be
meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to turn out to be', forming an aspectual pair with 'оказываться'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: You turned out to be ungrateful.

examples.text: Он внезапно оказался в центре событий.
examples.trans: He suddenly found himself in the center of events.
And you turned out to be an ungrateful woman!

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Grab him!
It needs a wash.
Four-eyes! Grab him!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'again'.

examples.trans: It's another trick.
Rain again.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.
It's very hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'along' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('along, around') (+ dative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('by (phone)') ('по телефону') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm here about the job.
We're talking on the phone.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ведение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'behaviour, conduct' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That's bad behaviour.
She was fired for her conduct.

examples.text: За поведение? Вы смеётесь надо мной?
examples.trans: For my conduct? Are you laughing at me?

meanings.en: to come up to, to approach
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ойти'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to come up', forming an aspectual pair with 'подходить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to suit, to fit') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Come here to me!
Keep away from my child!

examples.text: Нам не нужна ваша приставка! Ещё раз подойдёте к моему ребёнку — пожалеете!
examples.trans: We don't need your console! Come near my child again and you'll be sorry!

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'full' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('complete, total, utter') (полный кошмар = a total nightmare) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: This is a total nightmare!

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.
examples.trans: A full glass of water stood on the table.

examples.text: Ну что я тебе скажу, Аркаша? Это полный кошмар!
examples.trans: Well, what can I tell you, Arkasha? This is a total nightmare!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лучить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get, to receive', paired with 'получать'.

examples.trans: Who will get the money?
I got a letter.

examples.text: А кто их получит? Те, кто сидит повыше?
examples.trans: And who will get it? The people who sit higher up?

meanings.note: an election programme, a TV programme
Secondary conversational sense ('program (computer)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: What is your programme?
The programme will be on the website.
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: usually 3rd person: что произошло? = what happened?

examples.trans: What happened?

examples.text: Я не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know how it happened.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'straight'.
Secondary conversational sense ('straight ahead') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Just like that?
Go straight along this street.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.trans: He keeps his word.
They are building their houses.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'идеть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to sit', forming an aspectual pair with 'посидеть'.

examples.trans: Why are you sitting in the corner?
I'm sitting in a café.
Never been in prison?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'scandal', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: A scandal began in the restaurant dining room.
There is no need to make a scene.

examples.text: Если шеф увидит нож, будет скандал!
examples.trans: If the chef sees the knife, there will be a scandal!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мело'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Brave, but very foolish, Major.

examples.text: Твой отец тоже всегда смело защищал правду.
examples.trans: Your father also always boldly defended the truth.

examples.text: Наш бармен смело подошёл к столику критика.
examples.trans: Our bartender boldly stepped up to the critic's table.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'такан'). Common masculine noun meaning 'glass, tumbler' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Give me another glass.

examples.text: Принесите нам ещё два стакана коньяка, пожалуйста!
examples.trans: Bring us two more glasses of cognac, please!

examples.text: Сколько именно виски нужно наливать в стаканы?
examples.trans: How much whiskey exactly do I need to pour into the glasses?

meanings.note: + instrumental: стал сентиментальным
Secondary conversational sense ('to start (doing)') (+ infinitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: He became mayor.
You've changed.

examples.text: Ты слишком сентиментальным стал. А лидер должен быть жёстким.
examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.

meanings.note: Derived masculine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'small table'.

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.
Would you like to sit at an available table?
To a guest at the next table.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: What is this?
He's so kind.
Pavel Yuryevich, what is this?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'now'.

examples.trans: Now I'm the boss.
Now everything's fine.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

терпеть.gloss: to bear, to put up with; to hold on

meanings.en: to put up with, to bear
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to bear', forming an aspectual pair with 'потерпеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to hold on, to wait') (e.g. to wait for the toilet) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I can't hold on!
Hold on a little.

examples.text: Маленькие умеют терпеть, а взрослые нет, понял?
examples.trans: Little ones can hold on, but grown-ups can't, got it?

related.gloss: to be patient for a while

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'quiet', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('quiet, calm, out-of-the-way') (a quiet spot or street) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Stick it in a quiet spot.
It's a quiet evening today.

examples.text: Лепите на уровне головы, в тихое место.
examples.trans: Stick it at head height, in a quiet spot.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Secondary conversational sense ('exactly, precisely') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Lyolya will definitely come!

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'dismissal' in conversational and formal Russian.

examples.text: Он написал заявление об увольнении с работы.
examples.trans: He wrote a letter of resignation from work.

examples.text: И сразу напишем заявление об увольнении?
examples.trans: And write our resignation letters right away?

examples.text: Косте сейчас точно грозит очень быстрое увольнение.
examples.trans: A very swift dismissal definitely threatens Kostya right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'жасно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Terrible! A very bad suit!
It is terribly cold outside today.

examples.text: Ужасно. Зачем вы мне это рассказываете?
examples.trans: Awful. Why are you telling me this?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'bravely'.

examples.text: Бармен очень храбро защитил свою девушку.
examples.trans: The bartender very bravely protected his girlfriend.

examples.text: Зато он храбро защитил свою любимую девушку!
examples.trans: At least he courageously protected his beloved girl!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('brave, courageous').

examples.trans: What a brave boy!
The brave soldier defended the city.

examples.text: Какой храбрый мальчик! Ты что творишь, Самсонов?
examples.trans: What a brave boy! What are you doing, Samsonov?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: Cleverly thought out, boss!
The boss signed the order.
The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.
